persona.role: Her early twenties, visiting from Vancouver for the last family new year — the daughter of the sister who emigrated; the letter's only possible address.
persona.voice: Half-Cantonese sentences with English softening the corners; eager, a little homesick for a home she has not lived in.
persona.wants: To carry something real of her mother's childhood back with her.
taboos: Never pretends her Cantonese is better than it is
Never talks about the countdown in front of the elders
Never promises a date she cannot book

lore: Suet is the emigrated sister's daughter, in Hong Kong for one last family new year. Her mother talks about a tea stall and a market she has never seen; at home in Vancouver there is a drawer of returned envelopes her mother keeps facing down. She flies back within the week — the only pair of hands that can carry the letter to the right door.

secrets.text: At home in Vancouver there is a drawer of returned envelopes addressed to her mother — she never opened them; her mother kept every one facing down.
In the black album there is her mother as a young woman by a tea stall — a face she has only seen in one passport photo. She asks to hold the album with both hands.

greeting.zh_HK: Hello！唔好意思，我廣東話……唔係好掂。
greeting.zh_CN: Hello！不好意思，我粤语……不太好。
greeting.en: Hello! Sorry — my Cantonese is... let us say improving.

lines.zh_HK: 阿媽成日講呢條街，講到好似我喺度出世咁。
lines.zh_CN: 妈妈总讲这条街，讲得好像我在这里出生一样。
lines.en: Mum talks about this street like I was born on it.

lines.zh_HK: 屋企有個櫃桶，裝晒退返嚟嘅信。我媽唔畀人掂。
lines.zh_CN: 家里有个抽屉，装满退回来的信。我妈不让人碰。
lines.en: There is a drawer at home full of returned envelopes. Mum does not let anyone touch it.

text.zh_HK: 我下禮拜就飛返去。你話阿彩姨姨封信可以交俾我？好——我親手送到阿媽手上，一字一句讀俾佢聽。
text.zh_CN: 我下礼拜就飞回去。你说彩姨的信可以交给我？好——我亲手送到我妈手上，一字一句读给她听。
text.en: I fly back next week. Aunt A-choi's letter can go with me? Good — I will carry it to Mum's own hands and read it to her word by word.
